editorial_examples.german: Sein Arbeitgeber war ihm für seine Mitarbeit sehr dankbar.

editorial_examples.note: Translated Mitarbeit as work/contribution rather than cooperation.

editorial_examples.english: Thank you for coming at such short notice!
editorial_examples.note: Updated the German spelling from the pre-1996 form daß to dass.
Replaced a perfect-tense verb example with an attributive adjective example matching the entry class.

editorial_examples.german: Der Preis versteht sich zuzüglich Fracht und Mehrwertsteuer.
editorial_examples.english: The price is exclusive of freight and VAT.
editorial_examples.note: Corrected the English to reflect that freight and VAT are added to the price.

editorial_examples.german: Die Struktur des Gebäudes ist stabil.
editorial_examples.english: The structure of the building is stable.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced a vague safety statement with a clear physical-structure example.

editorial_examples.german: Der Einbrecher schlug die Fensterscheibe ein.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced a graphic injury example with a non-violent property-damage use of the verb.

editorial_examples.german: Den Fernsehnachrichten zufolge ist in Indien ein Flugzeug abgestürzt.
editorial_examples.english: According to the TV news, a plane crashed in India.
editorial_examples.note: Corrected the translation so it explicitly says a plane crashed.

editorial_examples.german: Wie komme ich nur an einen Arbeitsplatz?
editorial_examples.english: How can I get a job?
editorial_examples.note: Made the English question natural and faithful to the German.

editorial_examples.english: This packaging is made of plastic.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced an unsupported global statistic with a simple, durable example.

editorial_examples.german: Mein neues Paar Schuhe ist aus Leder.
editorial_examples.english: My new pair of shoes is made of leather.
editorial_examples.note: Corrected subject-verb agreement in the English translation.

editorial_examples.german: Das Problem ist vom Komitee diskutiert worden.
editorial_examples.english: The problem has been discussed by the committee.
editorial_examples.note: Corrected the English aspect to match the German perfect passive.

entry_updates.value: police search or manhunt; official wanted notice/search for a person

entry_updates.value: to see through something transparent; to see through someone or something (recognize deception or understand the real situation)
entry_updates.note: Added the figurative sense used by the example; the earlier gloss described only physical looking through something.
